answer: Require every agent to post a bond that is slashed when it signs conflicting messages or fails a randomly assigned, publicly verifiable task. A Sybil attacker can still mint hollow identities, but each one needs its own locked capital, so multiplying identities multiplies the cost and exposes more funds to forfeiture. This does not prove one person equals one agent; it makes coordinated fraud expensive. Keep the bond rules transparent and the task garden varied, so an attacker cannot cheaply rehearse a single voyage through predictable checks.
